thread:
Sasha: heads up — CI microbench failed on PR #13456: kv-cache-stress shows ~14% latency regression on the batcher path. CI link: https://ci.redwood/internal/13456/jobs/kv_stress :frowning:
Matt: saw it, thanks. Rerunning the job now.
ci-bot: rerun started (job 78910) — will post results when done.
Sasha: rerun completed and reproduced, same delta. Quick snapshot of the perf diff: `p50 +12%, p95 +24%, tokens/s -9%`
Ana: I pulled the perf artifact and ran a quick trace. Flamegraph points at a repeated CPU->GPU memcpy hotspot and a jump in kernel fallback counts for the small-seq path.
Jordan: PR touched the batch-sampler window + the kv eviction heuristic and also a tiny change in kernel-selector scoring (prio: prefer small-seq kernels when estimated batch < 8). Could be interaction.
Matt: can you paste the trace snippet? even a short profile helps.
Ana: sure — paste below (trimmed):
```
Flame: cpu_memcpy (30%) -> kv_evict (18%) -> batcher_slice (12%)
Kernel selects: fast_large_seq: 40% -> slow_small_seq: 60% (before: fast_large_seq ~70%)
KV misses per request: 0.12 -> 0.38 (3x)
```
Sasha: interesting — KV misses up a lot. My guess: smaller microbatches due to sampler change are increasing headroom and causing more frequent evictions (slab churn). Term "slab starvation" shows up in allocator logs: `slab_reclaims++` bursts.
Jordan: plausible. If microbatches shrink, we push more frequent KV writes/evicts and end up with smaller kernels chosen more often. That explains both memcpy hotspot and kernel fallback.
Matt: can we reproduce locally with an env var config? command I used: `./run_perf --bench kv_stress --cfg pr/13456.json`
Ana: I ran a focused scap_viz and added extra logging. Repro script: `tools/perf/local_runner --case kv_churn --batch-window 6 --evict-threshold 0.2` — reproduces the memcpy spike in ~30s.
Sasha: plan suggestion: revert the kernel-selector scoring tweak in the PR (keep sampler + eviction changes for separate follow-up), and add a CI microbench that simulates high-KV-churn to catch this.
Jordan: +1 to revert. Long term we should add a guard in the sampler to increase window when KV churn metric > X and also instrument slab allocator occupancy.
Matt: I'll open a revert patch for the kernel selector change and re-run CI. If revert passes, we can unblock the PR and track sampler/evict fixes in a follow-up.
Sasha: creating revert PR now — @matt can you watch CI? tagging @ana and @jordan for follow-ups.
deploy-bot: rollout blocked for release branch until perf-gate is green on kv_stress.
ci-bot: revert PR 13456-revert created and queued for CI (job 78911).
Ana: I'll add a perf unit test that simulates slab churn and bake a golden threshold for p50/p95. Also uploading the trace artifact to the ticket.
Jordan: I'll start a bisect across the PR commits to see if we can isolate the exact line that nudged eviction behavior (probably around the sampler change).
Sasha: thanks — emojis: :eyes: :shipit: on the revert + :memo: for follow-ups.
Matt: update: revert CI green locally, pushing to CI now. Will report back in this thread.
ci-bot: job 78911 finished — metrics show regression removed, p50 back to baseline.
Sasha: great. Marking this PR as blocked until follow-ups land. We'll schedule a deeper postmortem if the KV-churn test shows intermittent flakes.
Jordan: noted — I'll create an engineering note with root-cause hypothesis and attach the bisect artifacts.
Sasha: perfect, thanks team.
